Hi

This is the start to my journal, in which I will document my journey into reading the market.

But first a little about me.

After looking at some of the posts and threads in this forum I will consider myself a newbie, rookie, green behind the ears.

I've been interested in trading for about 18 months, and I can identify all the common errors a trader makes in myself.

The connection between my mind and my right index finger, which hits the trigger is often overruled by emotions.

About 3 months ago I started looking at PASR, I focused on candle formations on the HTF. Suddenly I found I was starting to make better decisions and I knew their was more to this.

My trading style is undefined at this stage, but I do tend to favor the HTF's as screen time is limited.

I've decided to take this learning and trading experience seriously, so I'm going to start at the beginning and work my way through all the material do all the homework and practice, practice till its instinctive.

Hopefully the teacher here can help me achieve this.

Thank you to all those people that make this site a reality, It is much appreciated!

Ok here is my first exercise I've done based on key levels SR.

What I found interesting while doing the exercise is that if you have to write down what you see, you start thinking about it a lot more than just looking at the chart.

Price open (1) and moved down breaking through the lower major level and continuing to the next major level, here it found strong support and retraced back passed its opening price to the higher major level where it found resistance and closed slightly below this level. This was a significant bullish move. The bullish momentum continued breaking through another major level and found resistance at 1.30400 (2) were it stalled for a day but then continued the bullish momentum breaking this major level as well. The price close just above the minor level (3) 1.30740. Price started ranging over the next few days between two major levels 1.31300 and 1.30400 before breaking down, and closing in no man’s land. (4) Price gained significant bullish momentum breaking the 1.31300 major level but found resistance at the next major level 1.31930. (5) Resistance was obviously very strong and price changed direction with a significant move downwards back to the previous day opening, in the process breaking through 2 major levels. It found support at level 1.29960. Price once again started ranging between 1.30400 and 1.31300 (question to self or others does this mean that these 2 levels are becoming more significant 1.30400 and 1.31300, this is the second time price is ranging between them?). (6) Price eventually moves down breaking the 1.30400 level and closing just below the next major level. (7) It continues down to find support at the next major level before retracing to close above its opening price. Price then tries to make a bullish move but fails and retraces back to close near its opening price. ( Price tries again to move up but finds resistance at 1.30400 before breaking this level which then triggers a significant rally up before price finds resistance at the major level 1.31930 (9). The next day price continues up but doesn’t make it to the next major level before it retraces forming a “falling star” candle formation (indicating to me a trend reversal). (10) Price does react to this formation and moves down to find support at level 1.30400 (we are back at 1.30400 interesting). Once again we find price ranging between 1.31300 and 1.30400 it tests the upper level 1.31300 before breaking it and moving up till it finds resistance at the next major level 1.31930 (11). A decision is made and price starts to fall breaking through 2 major levels before finding support just short of the 3rd major level and comes to close at about 1.30400. (12) The momentum continues down with price breaking through the 1.29970 level and finding support at 1.29500. We have a double top formation; price must break the 1.29500 level for the formation to be confirmed. (13) Price retraces back to the previous major level and eventually closes forming a doji candle (the market is unsure of direction). (14) A decision is made price moves down breaking the 1.29500 level and confirming the double top formation. Price continues down before finding some resistance at 1.28400

and eventually moves down to just short of 1.27900 levels (15). Ok I’m going to stop here and continue tomorrow. From this exercise it seems to me that the levels 1.30400 and 1.31300 are significant, or let’s say have more importance than the other levels at this stage in PA on the chart?

خب این اولین تمرین من است که بر اساس سطوح کلیدی SR انجام داده‌ام.

چیزی که در حین انجام تمرین برایم جالب بود این است که وقتی باید آنچه می‌بینی را بنویسی، خیلی بیشتر از فقط نگاه کردن به چارت درباره‌اش فکر می‌کنی.

قیمت باز شد و پایین رفت، سطح ماژور پایین‌تر را شکست و به سطح ماژور بعدی رسید؛ آنجا حمایت قوی پیدا کرد و برگشت، از قیمت باز شدنش گذشت و به سطح ماژور بالاتر رسید؛ آنجا مقاومت پیدا کرد و کمی زیر آن سطح بسته شد. این یک حرکت صعودی مهم بود. مومنتوم صعودی ادامه یافت، یک سطح ماژور دیگر را شکست و در 1.30400 مقاومت پیدا کرد ؛ یک روز آنجا متوقف شد ولی بعد مومنتوم صعودی را ادامه داد و این سطح ماژور را هم شکست. قیمت کمی بالای سطح مینور 1.30740 بسته شد. قیمت در چند روز بعد بین دو سطح ماژور 1.31300 و 1.30400 رنج زد، بعد شکست و در بیابان بسته شد. قیمت مومنتوم صعودی مهمی گرفت و سطح ماژور 1.31300 را شکست ولی در سطح ماژور بعدی 1.31930 مقاومت پیدا کرد. مقاومت واضحاً خیلی قوی بود و قیمت با یک حرکت نزولی مهم به سمت باز شدن روز قبل برگشت و در این مسیر 2 سطح ماژور را شکست. در سطح 1.29960 حمایت پیدا کرد. قیمت دوباره بین 1.30400 و 1.31300 رنج زد (سؤال از خودم یا دیگران: آیا این یعنی این دو سطح مهم‌تر می‌شوند؟ 1.30400 و 1.31300؛ این دومین بار است که قیمت بین آن‌ها رنج می‌زند؟). قیمت در نهایت پایین رفت، سطح 1.30400 را شکست و کمی زیر سطح ماژور بعدی بسته شد. پایین‌تر رفت تا در سطح ماژور بعدی حمایت پیدا کند، بعد برگشت و بالای قیمت باز شدنش بسته شد. سپس تلاش کرد حرکت صعودی کند ولی شکست خورد و برگشت و نزدیک قیمت باز شدنش بسته شد. دوباره تلاش کرد بالا برود ولی در 1.30400 مقاومت پیدا کرد؛ بعد این سطح را شکست که یک رالی مهم صعودی راه انداخت، تا قیمت در سطح ماژور 1.31930 مقاومت پیدا کرد . روز بعد قیمت ادامه داد بالا ولی به سطح ماژور بعدی نرسید و برگشت و الگوی کندلی «ستارهٔ دنباله‌دار» را ساخت (که به نظر من نشانهٔ برگشت روند است). قیمت به این الگو واکنش نشان داد و پایین رفت تا در سطح 1.30400 حمایت پیدا کند (دوباره برگشتیم به 1.30400، جالب). دوباره قیمت بین 1.31300 و 1.30400 رنج زد، سطح بالایی 1.31300 را تست کرد، آن را شکست و بالا رفت تا در سطح ماژور بعدی 1.31930 مقاومت پیدا کرد . تصمیمی گرفته شد و قیمت شروع به ریزش کرد، 2 سطح ماژور را شکست و کمی قبل از سطح ماژور سوم حمایت پیدا کرد و حدود 1.30400 بسته شد. مومنتوم نزولی ادامه یافت و قیمت سطح 1.29970 را شکست و در 1.29500 حمایت پیدا کرد. یک الگوی دوقلو تشکیل شده؛ برای تأیید الگو قیمت باید سطح 1.29500 را بشکند. قیمت به سطح ماژور قبلی برگشت و در نهایت با تشکیل کندل دوجی بسته شد (بازار در جهت مطمئن نیست). تصمیمی گرفته شد، قیمت پایین رفت، سطح 1.29500 را شکست و الگوی دوقلو را تأیید کرد. قیمت ادامه داد پایین تا در 1.28400 کمی مقاومت پیدا کرد و در نهایت تا کمی قبل از سطوح 1.27900 پایین رفت .

خب اینجا متوقف می‌شوم و فردا ادامه می‌دهم. از این تمرین به نظرم می‌رسد سطوح 1.30400 و 1.31300 مهم‌اند، یا بهتر بگویم در این مرحله از PA روی چارت اهمیت بیشتری از بقیهٔ سطوح دارند؟ 10 11 12 14 15

Last week I was traveling. On thursday night I didn't have an internet connection so I started drawing my own charts. I wanted to understand what was happening when price moved and why there would be a pool of orders left behind or consumed. I started to realize that RTM isn't as much about trading than it is about what the name says "Read The Market".

If I can identify key areas, If I can identify the significance of those area's, and if I can READ what pro money wants to do, then trading what I see will be easy. Over the last few weeks I've been a sponge to the information on this site. Now its time to put some

structure and learning goals to that information,

My journal is no long going to be about what trades I've taken, but more about what I see, how I read what I see. Later I'll come back to trading.

Hello in2forex,

When you hit some stumbling blocks it can actually be more productive to just walk away and do something else. Not focusing on a problem directly moves it from conscious to subconscious and that can be a more powerful and creative tool for problem solving. Scientists have even proven (finally) that walking helps problem solving - the issue at hand is there, but it's not prioritised - the chains are off that wonderful subconscious....

It seems that trading is full of stumbling blocks, no matter how far along the road you think you are! Matters aren't helped by the fact that it's based on probabilities - you can be right and lose money, and you can be wrong but make money. The contrary feedback from these two entirely different scenarios doesn't help you when you are trying to learn what is right-thinking and what is wrong-thinking.

Even if you spend many hours investigating Price Action on the left (an absolute must), it doesn't necessarily convert into success at the hard right edge. But it is definitely one of the building blocks of success. If you're having trouble at the hard right edge now it might pay you to go back to the left.

I don't know how you think through or solve problems, but it's usually best to identify them, state them, and break them down bite sized chunks to be solved. You will have noticed that this is a major part of how I approach things - it's got me this far, but I really am struggling with the next bit right now

attention when you look at a chart: if several people look at the same chart, they will all see different things! For instance:

1. Do you notice the peaks and troughs as price zigs and zags or do you just notice the general direction that price takes over time? 2. Do you notice horizontal levels where price reacts or do you notice diagonal lines? 3. Do you notice spikes from levels or clusters at levels?

Knowing what you automatically key in to might be the first step in working through your stumbling block. When reading others' journals remember that although everyone is pretty much doing the same thing here, they may describe it differently, and each may arrive at the same point by different paths: that is a reflection of those different thought processes we each have. You might find one person's way confusing because you just don't see things their way and you might gel with another's because you do! It might be that as your experience and knowledge grow the first person's way becomes more obvious! There is no right or wrong to this (all views are valid if they are long-term profitable) you just have to find and stick with what works for you and grow from there -another of those building blocks for success.

If you don't know what you key in to try what I did way way back. I took charts and drew 'random' lines on them (knowing I would necessarily apply some element of judgment: brains aren't good at random, they are pattern seekers). I looked at what converged on those lines. I rinsed and repeated this several times until I confirmed that I was generally identifying the same things each time. Then I built from that.

Hopefully there's something of use here, but good luck and good hunting.

Hello in2forex,

I thought I might pitch in seeing as you mentioned you were struggling with Compression. This is my take on it so it probably isn't "according to Hoyle", keep your pinches of salt to hand

Compression usually happens at the end of a Momentum Move (or some sort of main move). Buyers or sellers have thrust price - unopposed - in their chosen direction (either because they had the strength to overwhelm the opposition or the opposition was sorely lacking (each can have different implications)). Eventually they reach an area where opposition slowly increases - the Momentum Move is over but inertia (read late buying or selling) sees price continue in the same direction. The strength is slowly sapped out of this incursive move until there is none left and the opposition can now push price in their direction....

Compression should be self-defeating, that's why it's thought of as a leading 'indicator' as price approaches Supply or Demand. What you see is the law of diminishing returns in effect: each successive thrust depletes orders to support the move, sees less distance covered for the same effort, and drives price deeper into opposition, perhaps even convinces opposition they are witnessing increasing weakness so attracting more of the same. The very shape (wedge-like) expresses Compression!

But it is not really Compression (in the sense it is meant in RTM) until price can close within its confines - that is, we do not know whether it is consumption of orders or rejection of 'cheap' prices, until we know

. That is, price could just as easily

'compress' into Supply or Demand and then drive straight through it (there are many variables at play here).

Also, that price is likely to be turned back at the last place of strength (i.e. the transition from Momo to Compression) implies the beginning of ranging and perhaps a continuation of price in the same direction as Momo, but as with all things it doesn't have to be this way.

Compression examples (please note that a little poetic licence was used

):

What you were seeing on EURUSD is a Flag. There are some similarities and many differences between a Flag and Compression:

1. Both occur at the end of Momo (or some form of main move)

2. Compression continues with the Momo whereas the Flag goes against it, because... 3. Compression occurs going into opposition Supply or Demand whereas a Flag occurs after hitting it 4. This also means that when Compression eventually hits Supply or Demand it is still fresh whereas the Flag has already started depleting it, so... 5. On retracing through Compression price is likely to be turned back at the last place where strength was shown whereas once a Flag has completed its pull back (to a source from which the Momo or main move can continue) it is likely to drive through its own extreme and continue with the main move 6. But, the transition from Momo to Compression is a base of strength which might lead to support ranging, and that might lead to a continuation of the main move, so in the end the outcome might be the same for both Compression and Flag even though the mechanism is different 7. Both deplete orders within their structures, removing obstacles to any move through them 8. Oh, and Compression is generally wedge-shaped whereas Flags form equidistant channels

As I say, there are several similarities between Compression and Flags, not least that as each rises to Supply (or falls to Demand) it absorbs buy (sell) orders, creating weakness within its structure, allowing price to move through it with relative ease (if that is the direction that price then takes). But there are important differences which prepare us to anticipate different Price Action after we see them: after Compression price might range in a PAZ before making its next move (possibly continuing in the same direction as the main move); after a Flag price might just shoot through and continue on in what's called a measured move (the first 'CP' example in your chart above shows this, so does Redsword11's example on page 19).

It's a shame that Redsword11's example doesn't capture what happened after the CP, but there are other examples from page 20 onwards which not only blur the definition of Compression but show price ranging after it. None of these things is set in concrete, and anything can and will happen - it's all about the next candle! And, of course, reference time-frame is important, so while your H1 example shows two Flags (as I would call them), they are part of a larger structure on H4 and D1 (in this case a range). It's sometimes difficult to decide what you're seeing and what you should pay most attention to....

In the end, as long as you know what you mean by Compression, and what you anticipate could happen after, that's what matters most.:)

Putting all that to one side, I'm not entirely sure I understand what you mean when you say your "main challenge is very often what looks like compression to me on the HTF doesn't translate to compression in the LTF". Very valid question, it shows me that you are really looking at the market in total. Concentrating on entries and exits are both as important as the other, the only difference for me is that when in a trade different aspects of emotions start to play on your mind. Learning to control these, is as important as choosing a good entry or exit. Enough rambling.

To answer your question, i'm going to run through the process I went through in making the trade As I have mentioned previously in my journal, I have had to change the way I trade due to other commitments which have reduced my chart time to almost zero.

This trade was based on a total of about 5 minutes of screen time.

Entry: On Friday morning I open about 5 pairs of charts all HTF and flicked through them looking for something to jump out at me. On the GBPJPY I saw the Cap and compression (A good looking can can in development). I drew in some rectangles noticing the ENG (1) and the FL(3) set my PO at that level and my stop loss above a higher FTR which you can see in the LTF). At this point I was only interested in a reaction and price falling through the CP. I didn't set a TP. I thought I'll check on the trade later during the day just before NFP new which was due out at about 14h30 my time. As it worked out I never got a chance to look at the chart again until after the market had closed on Friday night. When I did open the chart I notice the PO had been triggered and the reaction to my entry was perfect, price had reached the FTR you mention in your chart. I would have loved to exit then and I was kicking myself for not setting a TP. I couldn't do anything as the market was closed. Exit:: I thought of waiting for the market to open and then exit the trade but this was a demo trade (sleep was a reasonable priority) so I thought let me let it run. When I woke up I check the chart, price had engulfed up. I then did something I try avoid, I looked at the trade profit and that was a good enough reason to exit considering I wasn't able to manage the trade on a real time bases.

So in conclusion the exit of this trade was based on emotion and not PA. In the past my general strategy has been to exit a trade when I'm confident to take a trade in the opposite direction based on PA. Due to my current screen time limitations I can't do this now. So I'm having to change how I trade. This is just another learning curve on the journey to success.. I'm still struggling with the emotional stress when in a trade and often find myself looking at the profit, hence why I'm trying to avoid this.

Sorry for the long post, hope it helped. Now I need to get back to work.

برای پاسخ به سؤالت، روندی را که برای این معامله طی کردم مرور می‌کنم. همان‌طور که قبلاً در ژورنالم گفتم، به‌خاطر تعهدات دیگر مجبور شدم روش تریدم را عوض کنم که زمان چارت من را تقریباً به صفر رسانده است.

این معامله مجموعاً بر اساس حدود 5 دقیقه زمان صفحه بود.

ورود: جمعه صبح حدود 5 جفت چارت HTF باز کردم و آن‌ها را ورق زدم دنبال چیزی که به من فریاد بزند. روی GBPJPY کپ و کامپرشن را دیدم (یک Can قشنگ در حال شکل‌گیری). چند مستطیل کشیدم و اینگالف و FL را متوجه شدم؛ PO را روی آن سطح و حد ضرر را بالای یک FTR بالاتر گذاشتم که می‌توانی در LTF ببینی. در این نقطه فقط به واکنش و افت قیمت از CP علاقه‌مند بودم. TP نگذاشتم. فکر کردم بعداً در طول روز، درست قبل از خبر NFP که حدود 14h30 به وقت من بیرون می‌آمد، سر چارت نگاه می‌کنم. همان‌طور که شد، دیگر فرصت نشد تا بعد از بسته‌شدن بازار در جمعه شب چارت را ببینم. وقتی چارت را باز کردم متوجه شدم PO فعال شده و واکنش به ورودم کامل بوده؛ قیمت به FTR‌ی که در چارتت ذکر کردی رسیده بود. عاشق این بودم که همان‌جا خارج شوم و خودم را به‌خاطر نگذاشتن TP سرزنش می‌کردم. کاری نمی‌توانستم بکنم چون بازار بسته بود. خروج:: فکر کردم صبر کنم بازار باز شود بعد از معامله خارج شوم، ولی این یک معامله دمو بود (خواب اولویت معقولی بود) پس فکر کردم بگذارید بدود. وقتی بیدار شدم چارت را چک کردم؛ قیمت اینگالف صعودی کرده بود. بعد کاری کردم که سعی می‌کنم از آن پرهیز کنم: نگاه کردم به سود معامله و همین برای خروج در شرایطی که نمی‌توانستم معامله را به‌صورت real-time مدیریت کنم دلیل کافی بود.

پس در جمع‌بندی، خروج این معامله بر اساس احساس بود نه PA. در گذشته استراتژی کلی من این بود که وقتی مطمئن باشم بر اساس PA می‌توانم معامله در جهت مخالف بگیرم، از معامله خارج شوم. به‌خاطر محدودیت‌های فعلی زمان صفحه نمی‌توانم این کار را بکنم، پس مجبورم روش تریدم را عوض کنم. این فقط یک منحنی یادگیری دیگر در مسیر موفقیت است… هنوز با استرس احساسی داخل معامله دست‌وپنجه نرم می‌کنم و اغلب خودم را در حال نگاه‌کردن به سود پیدا می‌کنم؛ برای همین دارم سعی می‌کنم از این پرهیز کنم.
